papers.title: Utilization of Active Learning Strategies of the English Teachers of Public Elementary Schools in Malasiqui II District
papers.abstract: This study sought to determine the extent to which the English teachers of public elementary schools in Malasiqui II District during the School Year 2026-2027 are utilizing active learning strategies through a quantitative-descriptive-correlational research design. The data used in this study came from the 157 English teachers and 28 school heads which were subjected to frequency count, percentage, weighted mean, the chi-square test of independence, Pearson r, and regression analysis. Results showed that: majority of the English teachers have no post graduate degrees, have been teaching for more than ten years, and have attended not more than three trainings related with active learning; the English teachers perceived that they are almost always utilizing active learning strategies as evidenced by the computed overall weighted mean of 4.10 while the school heads perceived that the English teachers are only sometimes utilizing active learning strategies as evidenced by the computed overall weighted mean of 3.05; there is a significant relationship between the highest educational attainment, the length of teaching experience, and the number of relevant trainings attended of the English teachers and the extent to which they are utilizing active learning strategies; there is a significant difference between the perceptions of the English teachers and their schools on the extent to which the English teachers are utilizing active learning strategies; and, the English teachers have positive attitude towards active learning. Based from the findings, the following conclusions were drawn: a typical English teacher of a public elementary school in Malasiqui II District has no post-graduate degree, has been teaching for more than 10 years already, and has attended not more than three trainings related with active learning; the English teachers perceived that they are frequently using active learning strategies while the school heads perceived that the English teachers are utilizing active learning once in a while; the extent to which the English teachers are utilizing active learning strategies is influenced by their highest educational attainment, length of teaching experience, and the number of relevant trainings attended; the perceptions of the English teachers and the school heads on the extent to which the English teachers are utilizing active learning strategies are significantly different from each other; and, the attitude of the English teachers towards active learning may be capitalized as one of the bases for the proposed enhancement program.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文是小学英语教师教学策略的教育学调查，与FEA及代理建模方向完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This is an education survey on active learning strategies with no simulation, surrogate modeling, FEA, or biomechanics content whatsoever.

summary_zh.motivation: 调查小学英语教师使用主动学习策略的程度。
summary_zh.method: 采用定量描述相关设计，对157名教师和28名校长进行问卷与统计分析。
summary_zh.result: 教师与校长对策略使用程度的感知存在显著差异，且受学历与培训影响。
summary_zh.validation: 基于问卷数据的统计检验（卡方、回归）。

summary_en.motivation: The study examines how extensively elementary English teachers employ active learning strategies.
summary_en.method: A quantitative-descriptive-correlational design surveyed 157 teachers and 28 school heads, analyzed via chi-square, Pearson r, and regression.
summary_en.result: Teachers and school heads differed significantly in perceived strategy use, which correlated with educational attainment and training.
summary_en.validation: Statistical hypothesis testing on questionnaire survey data.
